You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in an orthorhombic input cell with lattice parameters a = 4.677544 Å, b = 9.804695 Å, and c = 9.963082 Å, with all three interaxial angles equal to 90°. The declared input composition comprises four silver, four mercury, four sulfur, and four bromine atoms, sixteen atoms in total, and the symmetry is that of space group number 51, Pmma (Hall symbol −P 2a 2a). All atomic positions are given as fractional coordinates, and the input and standard crystallographic frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the transformation matrix P has rows approximately (0, 0, 1), (1, 0, 0), and (0, 1, 0)—the tiny off-diagonal entries of order 10⁻³² or 10⁻³³ are numerical noise—and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0) to the same numerical precision. In effect, the standard frame's first axis corresponds to the input cell's c axis, the standard second axis to the input a axis, and the standard third axis to the input b axis, with no origin displacement, so the original input cell is recovered by applying the inverse permutation. Coordinate values are reported rounded to six decimal places, and no positional corrections beyond this rounding are required.

In the standard Pmma frame, the silver atoms occupy the fourfold Wyckoff position 4i with coordinate relation (x, 0, z), the representative atom sitting at x = 0.084788, y = 0, z = 0.209328; the four symmetry-equivalent silver atoms thus lie on the mirror plane at y = 0. Mercury is distributed over two inequivalent twofold orbits: one on site 2f with fixed coordinates (1/4, 1/2, z) and free parameter z = 0.770700, and a second on site 2d at the fixed position (0, 1/2, 1/2) with no free parameters. The sulfur atoms occupy the fourfold site 4j with relation (x, 1/2, z), represented by x = 0.008329, y = 1/2, z = 0.745748, so the four sulfurs lie on the mirror plane at y = 1/2. Bromine likewise occupies two crystallographically independent orbits, both of the same Wyckoff type 2e with relation (1/4, 0, z): one with z = 0.987567 and the other with z = 0.464781, each contributing two symmetry-related bromine atoms.

Taken together, the multiplicities of these six independent orbits—four silver, two plus two mercury, four sulfur, and two plus two bromine—sum to the sixteen atoms of the input cell and reproduce the declared Ag₄Hg₄S₄Br₄ composition. All atoms reside on special positions of Pmma: the silver and sulfur orbits lie on the two distinct mirror planes perpendicular to the second standard axis, while the mercury and bromine orbits sit at fixed x = 1/4 or x = 0 with y fixed at 0 or 1/2, their only freedom being the z coordinates specified above. With the lattice dimensions, the frame permutation, and these independent positional parameters, the complete atomic geometry of the original input cell is fully determined.
